source: Original 1672 × 941 transparent painting generated from the following prompt for this project. No outside source imagery.
prompt: Create a precision GAME TERRAIN SURFACE TRIM ATLAS on genuinely TRANSPARENT background. Canvas wide 16:9. FOUR separated narrow horizontal strips in four equally spaced rows. Each strip runs off BOTH left and right edges; all four rows stay completely separate with a transparent gutter. SIDE VIEW with a little top plane visible as in a handcrafted 2.5D pixel platformer. These are surface overlay trims laid along the FRONT LIP of playable terrain, NOT deep blocks and NOT background landscapes. Deliberately varied thin continuous tops with a few tiny irregular rocks and attached vegetation. Natural broken upper outline and ragged shallow lower outline with occasional hanging roots or moss and exposed layers. Literal ground contact at about lower middle of each strip: modest cool reflected light on the front, controlled moonlit pixels along rear edges. Material should read like sculpted 3D forms reduced to clean richly painted retro pixel clusters, clear high-value facets among deep indigo shadows. No giant props or tall bushes, no characters, no platforms detached from the strip. Row 1: weathered warm umber EARTH path from a Vietnamese rice village, uneven loam, scattered low rounded grey stones embedded in soil, intermittent clumps of golden-green field grass, sprouting weeds and earth crumbs, no bricks. Row 2: cool JADE BAMBOO FOREST trail of velvety emerald moss, very short ferns and fallen narrow bamboo leaves twisted over irregular root ledges, wet dark earth. Row 3: Vietnamese old RIVER QUAY of substantial hand-laid rectangular blue-grey blocks with CHIPPED and slightly uneven cap stones, moss between selected joints, small trails of ivy over the face, wet silver glints, strong sense of weight. Row 4: old BANYAN HILLSIDE with violet slate ledges, grey and umber roots clearly anchored in soil with one or two roots twisting along the top, copper moss and worn exposed stone chips. Each row contains broad gentle stretches between small, asymmetrically spaced detail clusters. No lighting halo, no ground shadows on the transparent background, no frame, no typography, no labels. Absolutely no sky/faraway scenery. Every row should be about one eighth to one sixth of canvas height; thin horizontal geometry so it tiles well, each row clearly separated above and below from the next.
processing: Four alpha trims share one sheet. A minimum-error seam over 144 source pixels joined the horizontal edges, producing a periodic 1528 × 941 texture. Alpha remains in the published asset. TerrainRelief.shader samples painted crests at the physical ground line, combined with the original four body textures documented in terrain-sources.json. TerrainArt generates exposed end bevels, weathered silhouettes and shelf undersides. The level geometry drives all mesh positions.
